BACKPORT: media: platform: Switch to v4l2_async_notifier_add_subdev Switch all media platform drivers to call v4l2_async_notifier_add_subdev() to add asd's to a notifier, in place of referencing the notifier->subdevs[] array. These drivers also must now call v4l2_async_notifier_init() before adding asd's to their notifiers. There may still be cases where a platform driver maintains a list of asd's that is a duplicate of the notifier asd_list, in which case its possible the platform driver list can be removed, and can reference the notifier asd_list instead. One example of where a duplicate list has been removed in this patch is xilinx-vipp.c. If there are such cases remaining, those drivers should be optimized to remove the duplicate platform driver asd lists. None of the changes to the platform drivers in this patch have been tested. Verify that the async subdevices needed by the platform are bound at load time, and that the driver unloads and reloads correctly with no memory leaking of asd objects. Suggested-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Steve Longerbeam <slongerbeam@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit d079f94c90469f413920b9f2b201537fac2ceb06) BUG=chromium:967723 TEST=allyesconfig Change-Id: I3a96b30301c885b75bee997c74c8bdbf57b532fc Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1631141 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Zubin Mithra <zsm@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: media: staging/imx: Loop through all registered subdevs for media links The root imx-media notifier no longer sees all bound subdevices because some of them will be bound to subdev notifiers. So imx_media_create_links() now needs to loop through all subdevices registered with the v4l2-device, not just the ones in the root notifier's done list. This should be safe because imx_media_create_of_links() checks if a fwnode link already exists before creating. Signed-off-by: Steve Longerbeam <slongerbeam@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 1488c3cf4f3ceaad1bad63898b4b4186f912f216) BUG=chromium:967723 TEST=allyesconfig Change-Id: I1615695664851db93215dd3fc1fdeda39d55c8c9 Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1631142 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Zubin Mithra <zsm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: media: staging/imx: Switch to v4l2_async_notifier_add_*_subdev Switch to v4l2_async_notifier_add_*_subdev() when adding async subdevs to the imx-media root notifier. This removes the need to check for an already added asd, since v4l2_async_notifier_add_*_subdev() does this check. Also no need to allocate a subdevs array when registering the root notifier, or keeping an internal master asd_list, since this is moved to the notifier's asd_list. vboot: save GBB header in workbuf during firmware verification Since GBB header will be needed for subsequent GBB reads later on (in kernel verification stage), and since GBB header is relatively small (128 bytes), save the full GBB header onto workbuf during firmware verification stage, and store an offset pointer to it in vb2_shared_data. vb2_gbb_header object may be accessed via the vb2_get_gbb function. Additionally, update functions in firmware/lib/region-init.c to read GBB data from flash, rather than using cparams passed in by depthcharge, which is slated for deprecation. BUG=b:124141368, chromium:954774 TEST=make clean && make runtests BRANCH=none Change-Id: I6e6218231299ce3a5b383663bc3480b20f929840 Signed-off-by: Joel Kitching <kitching@google.com> Cq-Depend: chromium:1585500 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1627430 Commit-Ready: Joel Kitching <kitching@chromium.org> Tested-by: Joel Kitching <kitching@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Joel Kitching <kitching@chromium.org>

power: Refactor: Add suspend_for to powerd_dbus_suspend. Previously when wakeup_timeout is passed to powerd_dbus_suspend, the script used to set the alarm immediately. As part of crrev.com/c/1517064 the wakeup_timeout is now passed to powerd to reduce spurious failures in suspend_stress_test when chrome took little longer to suspend. vm_tools: Notify chrome about pending app list updates This CL adds a new signal that notifies chrome about any pending app list updates. This allows chrome to decide if it should tell the user the operation has finished as soon as the packagekitd transaction commits, or if it should wait until it gets the updated app list. This allows us to synchronise the completion message in the UI with the (dis)appearence of app icons in the launcher. FIXUP: FROMLIST: USB: dwc2: Don't turn off the usbphy in suspend if wakeup is enabled === This is a revert of v2 of the patch that we landed FROMLIST squashed with a pick of v3. See CL:1593684 for v2. === If the 'snps,need-phy-for-wake' is set in the device tree then: - We know that we can wakeup, so call device_set_wakeup_capable(). The USB core will use this knowledge to enable wakeup by default. - We know that we should keep the PHY on during suspend if something on our root hub needs remote wakeup. This requires the patch (USB: Export usb_wakeup_enabled_descendants()). Note that we don't keep the PHY on at suspend time if it's not needed because it would be a power draw. If we later find some users of dwc2 that can support wakeup without keeping the PHY on we may want to add a way to call device_set_wakeup_capable() without keeping the PHY on at suspend time. CHROMIUM: mm: totmaps: split PSS into components This gives us separate numbers for PSS anon, file, and shmem. We need this to measure types of usage by process group.
